findings.claim: The manifesto now points at a test that no longer exists and still calls I11 planned. I10 cites test_minio_backup_syncs_a_declared_bucket, which the change renamed to test_minio_backup_syncs_declared_buckets. I11 says 'planned' and that the ticket 'widens the job', but this change built it and test_minio_backup_syncs_the_durable_buckets now enforces it. .okf/summary.md lines 69-70 also say the backup jobs 'do not have yet' a copy of every durable bucket.

Several pages still say only openviking is backed up, or describe this ticket as future work. In .okf/components/gcs-backups.md the 'Planned, not built' section describes this ticket as unbuilt. Its 180-day trap quotes the reference page as calling the rule 'a safety net for orphaned objects', a sentence this change removed. 'The marker flags fix that from the next run' is also out of date, since the run has happened. The same claim is in .okf/components/minio.md:141 ('Only one bucket is backed up'), .okf/components/container-registry.md:114 ('Not backed up'), .okf/nodes/orangepi4a.md:127, docs/how-to/run-a-backup-job-on-demand.md:65 ('syncs the openviking bucket') and the generated line in .okf/components/index.md:15, which kmctl check --fix regenerates.

SYNC_LINE matches only the exact 'rclone sync minio:X gcs:${gcs_bucket}/minio/Y/ ...' shape, and every check iterates over its matches. A fifth sync in another shape is invisible to the set-equality check, as are a sync with the flags before the destination or one that is not the last command on its line. The same goes for a bucket copied with 'rclone copy'. Count every 'rclone (sync|copy)' occurrence in the args and assert it equals the number of SYNC_LINE matches, so an unmatched command fails the test instead of slipping past it.

verdict.text: The jobspec change is correct and was proven live.
It runs four syncs, each with `|| rc=1` and both marker flags, and ends with `exit $rc`.
Every bucket is attempted, and any failure fails the task.
The deployed run exited 0, and the per-key comparison shows all four buckets fully in GCS.
What blocks a pass is consistency.
The manifesto cites a renamed test and still calls I11 planned, and five other pages still say only openviking is backed up.
These are plain text fixes, so none of them blocks.
Gates: I ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree.
Result: `pass gate pre_commit`, `pass gate cli_tests`, `pass eval-row r1`, `stamp green: d1abcc95545281d0d1e91e6a7616eab45c192b4572b41b109378c121e91e0217`.
`tests/test_backup_coverage.py` reported 8 passed.
r1: I read the tests.

`test_minio_backup_syncs_the_durable_buckets` compares the sorted source list with the four names, so an extra bucket, a missing one or a duplicate fails it, and it checks that each destination prefix equals its source.
`test_minio_backup_syncs_declared_buckets` checks each source against `local.buckets`.
Each case in fails_when is asserted, within the limit in f3.
r2 (judgment): `/bin/sh -c` runs four lines, each `rclone sync ... || rc=1`, with no `set -e` and no `&&`.
A failed sync sets rc=1 and the next line still runs.
`exit $rc` exits nonzero if any sync failed.
`test_minio_backup_fails_when_any_sync_fails` pins `|| rc=1` on every line, `rc=0` and `exit $rc`.
In templatefile, `$rc` without braces passes through unchanged, which the live run confirms.
Met.
r3 (judgment): allocation 8e84a792 ended complete with exit 0, recorded in the spike 2 and 3 READMEs.
I read spike 3's `compare.py` and `stdout.txt`.
For each bucket it lists both sides and compares every file key and size.
It also checks that every MinIO directory key has a directory in GCS.

Results: openviking 37,137 files and 836,331,631 B on both sides, registry 399 files and 5,340,847,012 B on both sides, models and datalake empty on both sides, with 0 missing, 0 differing and 0 directories lost.
The check is one-way, but equal file counts on both sides rule out extra files in GCS.
That is stricter than equal `rclone size` totals, so I accept it in place of the eight `rclone size` outputs.
Object counts differ only because of directory markers, which the README explains.
Met.
r4 (judgment): `docs/reference/gcs-backups.md` lists the four buckets and says that an object unchanged for 180 days is deleted and uploaded again the next night.
`.okf/components/gcs-backups.md` lists the four in its description and coverage section and keeps the 180-day trap for each `minio/<bucket>/` prefix.
Met.
Other pages fall short, see f1 and f2.
Code read: the full diff and the full text of all five changed files, plus a grep of docs/ and .okf/ for backup claims that are now stale.
f1 (docs, non-blocking): manifesto I10 names `test_minio_backup_syncs_a_declared_bucket`, which no longer exists.
I11 still says planned.
The summary says the widening has not happened yet.
f2 (docs, non-blocking): the 'Planned, not built' section and the 'safety net' quote in `.okf/components/gcs-backups.md` are now false.
minio.md, container-registry.md, orangepi4a.md, the how-to's Step 4 prose and the components index still say only openviking is backed up.
f3 (test-strength, non-blocking): a sync line outside the regex's exact shape escapes every check.
Assert that every `rclone sync` or `rclone copy` in the args was parsed.
Spike 3 found that registry got 725 directory markers in GCS that MinIO never had.
A restore with `--s3-directory-markers` would create those keys in SeaweedFS.
That belongs to the cutover ticket, but it would be worth a line in the gcs-backups traps so it does not live only in a spike.
